# 5-Condition Factorial Run — Results Analysis

**Date:** 2026-05-12
**Source:** 15 runs (5 conditions × 3 seeds) under `experiments/5cond_factorial/multi_condition_ablation/`
**Auto-analysis:** `experiments/analysis_outputs/5cond_component0/` (regenerated by `compare_5conditions.py`)
**Sister files in this trilogy:**
- `architecture_analysis.md` — why the graph/feature variants underperform
- `testing_framework_proposal.md` — how to fix the testing protocol going forward

---

## TL;DR

| Cond | Median NSE | Median KGE | Median log-NSE |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L** — NH `cudalstm` baseline | **0.653** | **0.728** | **0.683** |
| G — DirectedGraphLSTM, empty edges, no topo features | 0.609 | 0.515 | 0.622 |
| G+T — + topology features (no msgs) | 0.605 | 0.512 | 0.616 |
| G+M — + message passing (no topo) | 0.583 | 0.559 | 0.605 |
| G+T+M — both | 0.586 | 0.533 | 0.604 |

**The paper-claim direction is REVERSED.** Every "advanced" condition (G+T, G+M, G+T+M) underperforms even the simplest no-graph baseline (G), which itself underperforms cudalstm (L) by ≈ 0.050 NSE.

The dominant cause is **NOT** what we previously thought. The L vs G gap is overwhelmingly a **training-budget confound**, not an architecture confound. See `architecture_analysis.md` for the mechanism; this document focuses on what the data say.

---

## 1. Numbers in detail

### 1.1 Cross-seed stability — tight enough to trust

| Cond | NSE per seed (11/13/17) | std across seeds |
|---|---|---|
| L | 0.653 / 0.651 / 0.656 | 0.002 |
| G | 0.609 / 0.614 / 0.590 | 0.013 |
| G+T | 0.605 / 0.613 / 0.603 | 0.005 |
| G+M | 0.583 / 0.611 / 0.581 | 0.017 |
| G+T+M | 0.586 / 0.596 / 0.578 | 0.009 |

Cross-seed std is **0.002–0.017 NSE** — an order of magnitude smaller than the between-condition gaps. The 3-seed design is statistically adequate for the contrasts we care about.

### 1.2 The six pairwise contrasts (paired per basin × seed, n=549, NSE)

| Contrast | Median Δ | 95% bootstrap CI | n strongly + (Δ ≥ 0.05) | n strongly − (Δ ≤ −0.05) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L − G** | **+0.050** | **[+0.042, +0.058]** | **275** | 77 |
| (G+T) − G | −0.001 | [−0.002, +0.001] | 30 | 25 |
| (G+M) − G | −0.006 | [−0.010, −0.001] | 60 | 103 |
| (G+T+M) − (G+T) | −0.014 | [−0.019, −0.010] | 60 | 142 |
| (G+T+M) − (G+M) | −0.007 | [−0.010, −0.004] | 33 | 60 |
| (G+T+M) − G | −0.011 | [−0.016, −0.007] | 66 | 138 |
| Interaction T×M | −0.009 | [−0.013, −0.006] | 49 | 72 |

**Reading:**

- **L − G dwarfs everything else.** It is 5× the size of the next-largest effect.
- **Topology features alone (G+T − G) are null.** 30 basins strongly positive vs 25 strongly negative. Pure noise.
- **Message passing alone (G+M − G) is slightly net-negative.** Hurts 103 basins, helps 60. Not a wash; a small loss.
- **Combining T and M is worse than either.** G+T+M − G is the most negative pairwise contrast at −0.011. The combination is *sub-additive*: interaction term is significantly < 0.
- **Adding messages on top of topology** (G+T+M − G+T = −0.014) is the most damaging single move in the design space.

### 1.3 Per-basin pattern is broad, not bimodal

For L vs G, averaging across seeds:
- 76% of basins prefer L; 50% strongly so (Δ > +0.05)
- 10% of basins strongly prefer G (Δ < −0.05)
- Per-basin std of (L − G) is 0.093

This is the signature of a **systemic optimization-side issue** that affects most basins uniformly, not a basin-class-specific architectural mismatch. A real architectural problem (e.g., "DirectedGraphLSTM is wrong for low-flow basins") would produce a bimodal distribution.

### 1.4 Stratifications

**Depth-stratified (Component 0 has depths 0/1/2/3/4 with 33/81/51/16/2 basins):**

The plot at `experiments/analysis_outputs/5cond_component0/nse_by_depth.png` shows L > G at every depth. The gap *narrows slightly* at depth 0 (headwaters, no upstream signal possible) and is largest at depth 1-2 — but the difference between strata is small. **Depth does not modulate the L − G gap much**, consistent with the training-budget interpretation (it should affect all depths equally).

**Area-stratified (small/medium/large terciles):**

Same pattern. No tercile shows G > L. The gap is similar across area classes.

### 1.5 Outlier-trimmed (drop bottom 5% of NSE per seed)

| Cond | Full median NSE | Trimmed median | Shift |
|---|---|---|---|
| L | 0.653 | 0.666 | +0.013 |
| G | 0.609 | 0.616 | +0.008 |
| G+T | 0.605 | 0.612 | +0.007 |
| G+M | 0.583 | 0.598 | +0.015 |
| G+T+M | 0.586 | 0.594 | +0.009 |

L has the *smallest* outlier penalty (shift +0.013 means few basins drag down its median), which means cudalstm's failures are less extreme than the graph variants'. **The graph variants have more catastrophically-bad basins** — likely the same undertrained-baseline story.

---

## 2. Loss trajectories — the smoking gun

From each run's `run_config.json` (G_seed11, all 4 graph variants):

```
        epoch  0    5    10   15   20   25   29
G:      loss  0.91 0.61 0.49 0.43 0.41 0.37 0.36
G+T:    loss  0.96 0.63 0.50 0.45 0.42 0.38 0.37
G+M:    loss  0.90 0.56 0.46 0.41 0.39 0.37 0.35
G+T+M:  loss  0.95 0.58 0.47 0.43 0.40 0.38 0.36
```

**Loss is still falling at epoch 30.** The 4-epoch trailing decline (epoch 25 → 29) is roughly 3% of the current loss, with no sign of plateau. Slope is approximately constant on a log scale from epoch ~10 onward — pure exponential decay with a long tail.

If you extrapolate naively (NSE rises ~0.05 per 0.05 loss reduction in this regime), full convergence would put G in the 0.65 range — i.e., parity with L. **The graph variants are not done training.**

---

## 3. Root cause: training-budget confound

NH `cudalstm` trainer (NeuralHydrology's default training loop):
- Samples random `(basin, window)` pairs of size `batch=256`
- Each basin × window is independent
- **~2,610 gradient updates per epoch** on Component 0 (183 basins × 3,652 windows / 256)
- 30 epochs × 2,610 ≈ **78,000 gradient updates**

DirectedGraphLSTM trainer (our `train_graph_component0.py`):
- Samples whole windows (each window contains *all 183 basins* simultaneously, because message passing requires inter-basin coupling)
- `batch=256` means 256 windows per step, each step touches all 183 basins
- **~14 gradient updates per epoch** (3,652 windows / 256)
- 30 epochs × 14 ≈ **420 gradient updates**

**Ratio: 186× fewer gradient updates over the same nominal "30 epoch" budget.**

This is the entire L − G story. Confidence on this is now high because:
1. Architecture audit (`architecture_analysis.md`) found no other meaningful difference.
2. The loss-curve evidence (still falling at epoch 30) directly shows incomplete convergence.
3. The per-basin uniformity of L > G matches an optimization confound, not an architecture confound.

---

## 4. What can be claimed from this run

### Defensible claims (the ones in scope for the paper *if we publish what we have*)

1. **Topology features add nothing on top of basin one-hot encoding.** G+T − G is statistically zero. This is a genuine finding: the per-basin one-hot already encodes "which basin am I" with sufficient capacity to subsume hand-designed topology summaries. Architectural reasons in §3 of `architecture_analysis.md`.
2. **At our training budget, message passing slightly hurts.** G+M − G = −0.006 with CI excluding zero. Not a wash; a small but real loss.
3. **Topology and message passing are sub-additive.** Interaction T×M = −0.009. They overlap rather than complement.
4. **The 23-basin pilot's +0.078 NSE does not replicate at Component-0 scale.** This was already known from the previous A/B/C run; this sweep confirms it with multi-seed rigor.

### Claims that are **NOT** defensible from this run alone

1. ❌ "Graph-LSTM hurts at scale" — false framing. **The actual finding is "DirectedGraphLSTM hurts when trained for 186× fewer gradient updates than the baseline."** Headline framing must change.
2. ❌ "cudalstm > DirectedGraphLSTM architecturally" — not testable from this run; needs a matched-budget comparison.
3. ❌ "The graph signal is not informative" — this only shows the graph signal *was not extracted* by the undertrained model, not that it doesn't exist.
4. ❌ Any positive paper claim that "our added features beat a standard LSTM" — we are losing on both axes (architecture-matched-control AND vs the cudalstm baseline) under the current design + training budget.

---

## 5. Implications for the paper

The current run results **cannot support the paper's intended thesis** ("our added features outperform standard LSTM"). Three honest paths forward:

**Path A — Fix training budget, re-run, hope to recover.** Most likely, training the graph variants to convergence will close the L − G gap. The interesting contrasts (G+T − G, G+M − G, G+T+M − G) are *small* (≤ 0.015 NSE) — they may swing in either direction once the baseline is properly trained. If after training G to convergence the graph contrasts STILL come out small/negative, the original "graph helps" thesis is dead on this dataset and we must pivot. (See `testing_framework_proposal.md` Step 1.)

**Path B — Re-design the message-passing and topology features.** Several architectural defects (basin-encoding subsumes topology features; mean aggregation discards per-edge importance; single linear message function; no validation-set best-checkpoint selection) plausibly cap the upside even with sufficient training. (See `architecture_analysis.md` sections 3 and 4.)

**Path C — Re-frame the paper.** If after both A and B the graph signal genuinely doesn't outperform cudalstm, the publishable finding is *"per-basin one-hot encoding makes hand-designed graph signal redundant at Component-0 scale"* — a substantive negative finding with implications for the GNN-on-rivers literature.

The order should be **A → B → (decide on C)**. A is cheap (one matched-budget run); B is moderate (a re-designed sweep). If both improve the picture, we have a paper. If neither does, we have C.
